project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
New Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS): the software platforms distribution system operators (DSOs) use to monitor and control their grids, built on vendor-agnostic reference architectures.
The project must design and test innovative solutions, architectures, technologies and processes for how ADMS are designed and operated, so that DSOs can control their grids better, integrate distributed energy resources (DERs, such as solar panels, batteries, heat pumps and charging points) and manage congestion. The call writes the acronym both as ADSM and ADMS; it means the same system.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Projects are expected to address all six items the call lists; none is optional and the call names no excluded activities.
- Design and test innovative ADMS solutions, architectures, technologies and processes
- Provide ADMS software platforms that improve grid performance and controllability and integrate DERs efficiently, while reducing congestion and improving grid flexibility
- Improve forecasting of supply, demand and flexibility available to the system operator, with advanced analytics and visualisation
- Advance interoperability with transmission system operators (TSOs), with other DSOs and with DERs at the edge of the grid
- Use digital twins (live virtual models of the grid) and artificial intelligence, apply security-by-design and protection against cyber threats, and use or develop open-source software as far as possible
- Write a manual and best practices, including instructions to operate the system, for use by other DSOs, and identify remaining research and development gaps
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
The need lies with DSOs, who must run distribution grids with many more DERs, more congestion and more need for flexibility.
The call frames the problem as an operational one for distribution system operators: their grids must become more reliable, resilient, controllable and efficient while integrating distributed generation and new loads. The need therefore originates with operational users, the DSOs, and through them with grid users waiting for connection or facing congestion. TSOs share the need where the call asks for TSO-DSO interoperability.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
ADMS software platforms, vendor-agnostic reference architectures and tools, forecasting and analytics tools, interoperability solutions and a manual with best practices for other DSOs.
- ADMS software platforms tested and validated in at least two pilots
- Vendor-agnostic reference architectures, solutions and tools to manage a broad range of grid services
- Forecasting solutions for supply, demand and flexibility, with analytics and visualisations
- Interoperability solutions with TSOs, other DSOs and DERs
- Open-source software or modules where possible
- A manual with operating instructions and best practices, and a list of remaining gaps
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all three expected outcomes: more reliable, controllable distribution grids with congestion managed effectively, digitally equipped DSOs, and vendor-agnostic ADMS architectures.
- Enhanced reliability, resilience, controllability and efficiency of distribution grids, with congestion managed effectively
- DSOs use modern digital solutions to manage their grids and improve interoperability with TSOs and other DSOs
- Vendor-agnostic reference architectures, solutions and tools that advance ADMS design and operation and manage a broad range of grid services
The call sets no quantified targets.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The results are meant for wider use by other DSOs: the project must deliver a manual and best practices, and join the BRIDGE initiative.
- Transferability: the vendor-agnostic architecture, open-source software where possible, and the manual with operating instructions are meant for use by other DSOs
- Interoperability: the project must advance interoperability with TSOs, other DSOs and DERs
- Replication: validation in at least two pilots in different countries is required during the project; the call sets no replication target after it
- Knowledge sharing: selected projects are expected to contribute to BRIDGE (the European Commission's cooperation network of smart-grid, storage and digital energy projects) and take part in its activities
The call does not say who must operate or maintain the results after the project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
The topic also expects at least three DSOs and at least two universities or research organisations, so a realistic consortium has at least five partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
Projects are expected to include at least three DSOs and at least two universities or research organisations; a TSO is encouraged, not required.
The call encourages collaboration with:
- at least one supplier of ADMS technology and solutions
- at least one TSO whose grid connects to the grid of one of the partner DSOs
- at least one project funded under the parallel topic on advanced TSO control rooms (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-25), with a credible mechanism for that cooperation described in the proposal
These minimum numbers apply to the project as a whole, not to each pilot. Entities established in an eligible country but directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China are not eligible.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call prescribes no split of budget or work packages, but the demonstration must be spread over at least two pilots in different countries.
The demonstration, test and validation must be carried out in at least two pilots in different EU Member States or Associated Countries. The expected partner numbers apply to the project in total, not per pilot.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
The topic does not reserve the role, but with three DSOs expected and DSO pilots at the centre, a DSO or a research partner is the natural lead; this is our reading, not a rule.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but the project centres on DSO systems, so TenneT TSO B.V. would normally join as the encouraged TSO rather than lead.
Any beneficiary may be chosen as coordinator, and a Dutch entity is eligible. TenneT does not count towards the three expected DSOs. It must not be directly or indirectly controlled by China or a Chinese entity, an eligibility condition for this topic.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
The call encourages at least one TSO connected to a partner DSO's grid, without saying in which role; TenneT could fill this role as an associated partner if it wants no grant and only limited work.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a beneficiary filling the encouraged TSO role, TenneT can receive up to 70% of its eligible costs.
This topic is an innovation action (a project that develops, pilots and demonstrates new or improved solutions close to the market). The maximum rate is 70% for organisations other than non-profit legal entities, which applies to TenneT TSO B.V. The grant reimburses costs actually incurred plus a 25% flat rate for indirect costs. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 9.5 million per project, shared by all beneficiaries, so a TSO partner in a DSO-led project would likely receive a small share. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount, Budget categories
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT could be the TSO connected to Dutch partner DSOs, testing data exchange and flexibility coordination between transmission and distribution.
This is our interpretation. TenneT already coordinates with Dutch DSOs on congestion through the regional Energy boards and lets regional operators take part in its ARTeMIS balancing platform; TSO-DSO interoperability is where it would add most. It could also link the project to its own control-room work, such as the National Facility Digital Twin of the Electricity System, and to a project under the parallel TSO control-room topic. Its role would be supporting, since the call expects DSOs to lead the pilots.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
The project must deliver innovative ADMS solutions and architectures; it may build on existing digital twins and AI.
The scope asks to design and test innovative solutions and to advance forecasting and interoperability. The general award criteria assess how far the work goes beyond the state of the art.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 23 · D — Award criteria

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: A combination of technology (software platforms), system architecture (vendor-agnostic reference architectures) and operational methods (processes, operating instructions and best practices).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer:
Design, development, testing and validation in pilots; the call does not ask for full roll-out.
The project must design and test solutions and carry out demonstration, test and validation in at least two pilots, ending with a manual, best practices and identified research gaps.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 6–8 by the end of the project and may start at any TRL.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 8 is a complete and qualified system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer:
Demonstration, test and validation should take place in at least two pilots in different EU Member States or Associated Countries.
The call does not name the setting, but TRL 6–8 implies testing in a relevant to operational environment, in practice on the partner DSOs' grids or a close replica.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope and Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The ADMS must work with TSO systems, other DSOs and the DERs at the edge of the grid.
The project must link the ADMS platform with forecasting, DER integration and flexibility, and make it interoperable across operators. It must also cooperate with a project under the parallel TSO control-room topic, describing a credible mechanism in the proposal.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
The pilots must validate the solutions, but the call sets no indicators.
The evidence follows from the expected outcomes: better controllability and reliability, effective congestion management, efficient DER integration and interoperability with TSOs and other DSOs. The proposal must define the measures.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer:
Users are central: at least three DSOs, the operational users of ADMS, are expected in the consortium.
The call also encourages collaboration with an ADMS supplier and a connected TSO. It sets no specific co-design procedure.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
Security-by-design and advanced protection against cyber threats are required, and Chinese-controlled entities are excluded.
- Cybersecurity: the solutions must use security-by-design and advanced protection mechanisms against cyber threats
- Control restriction: entities directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China are not eligible, because this innovation action falls in a critical technology area
- Satellite data: if the project uses satellite-based earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing data, it must use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS (the EU satellite systems)
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 9–10 · B — Restrictions on control in Innovation Actions in critical technology areas

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission expects to fund about 3 projects of around EUR 9.5 million each, within a topic budget of EUR 28.5 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 9.5 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: actual-cost grant (reimburses eligible costs actually incurred) with a 25% flat rate for indirect costs
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 29, 31 · F — Budget flexibility; G — Form of grant

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant reimburses only eligible costs actually incurred, plus a flat 25% for indirect costs; subcontracting should stay a limited part.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchase costs (equipment, travel, other goods and services), plus personnel unit costs where the beneficiary uses them
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a flat rate of 25% of eligible direct costs, excluding subcontracting and financial support to third parties
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting should normally be a limited part of the project and be done by third parties, not by beneficiaries; purchases must give best value for money
Budgeted costs are not paid as such: only the costs actually incurred are reimbursed.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium roles

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 40 pages
- Opening: 4 August 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around May 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 40 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking, Budget flexibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The China-control restriction, the cooperation with the TSO control-room project and the satellite-data rule apply in addition to the general rules.
- Exception — entities controlled by China: an entity in an eligible country that is directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established there is not eligible
- Conditional — cooperation with the parallel TSO control-room topic: the proposal is expected to describe a credible mechanism for working with at least one project under HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-25
- Conditional — satellite data: if satellite earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing data are used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used
- Recommended: contribute to BRIDGE; collaborate with an ADMS supplier and a connected TSO
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-26, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 9–10 · B — Restrictions on control in Innovation Actions in critical technology areas
